title: Control trace matrix + decision tree and evidence queries
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook maps SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls to concrete evidence sources (RBAC v2, audit-log exports, SIEM indices, and automation hooks) and provides a decision tree for triaging auditor queries. It is intended for the security engineering and compliance teams to accelerate evidence collection, reduce back-and-forth with auditors, and prioritize remediation where the platform has gaps.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Controls related to access management, logging & monitoring, change control, and evidence retention that rely on RBAC v2 and audit-log exports.
- Audience: Security engineers, compliance owners, SREs supporting SIEM ingestion, and audit liaisons.

High-level summary of outputs (what this doc gives you):
1) A traceable mapping from control to evidence artifact and the primary index or query to retrieve samples.
2) A decision tree to answer auditor questions quickly (yes/no + evidence path).
3) A prioritized gap list with recommended tactical remediation and automation playbooks.
4) A short Q&A bank with suggested artifact screenshots/queries to attach for SOC 2 / ISO interviews.

Control trace matrix (narrative form - canonical controls -> evidence):
- Control: Access provisioning and deprovisioning (ISO A.9 / SOC2 CC6)
  Evidence sources: RBAC v2 change events (api: /rbac/v2/events), IAM provisioning audit-log index (siem: rbac-provisioning-*), user lifecycle CSV exports from identity provider (IdP).
  Primary retrieval query: siem> index=rbac-provisioning-* | where event_type in ("create-role","assign-role","revoke-role","deactivate-user") | sort by timestamp desc | head 50
  Key artifact examples: role binding delta JSON, approval ticket id (JIRA-SC-4821), timestamped webhook that triggered automation.

- Control: Principle of least privilege & role reviews (ISO A.9.2 / SOC2 CC6):
  Evidence sources: periodic role-review reports (platform-reporting: /reports/role-review), snapshot of effective permissions from RBAC engine, calendar invite of review meeting, attestation email.
  Primary retrieval query: platform-reporting> GET /reports/role-review?start=<date>&end=<date> -> csv
  Acceptance criteria: review contains reviewer, scope (roles checked), findings log, and remediation items with owners.

- Control: Authentication and session logging (ISO A.9.4 / SOC2 CC7):
  Evidence sources: auth-service audit logs (index: auth-logs-*), session creation/deletion events in rbactracer, SSO provider login history.
  Primary retrieval query: siem> index=auth-logs-* | where event in ("login_success","login_failed","logout") | stats count by user, outcome, hour

- Control: Immutable audit trail & tamper-detection (ISO A.12.4 / SOC2 CC7):
  Evidence sources: write-once S3 buckets with server-side encryption (s3://audit-immutable/), object-checksum manifest, SIEM ingest audit and checksum verification logs, signed export link.
  Primary retrieval query: storage> list objects s3://audit-immutable/period=2024-09/ | grep manifest && siem> index=ingest-audit | where object_key like "audit-immutable/%"

Decision tree for typical auditor questions (textual flow):
1) Auditor: "Show me a sample of role assignment and who approved it in the last 90 days."
   - Step A: Query siem index rbac-provisioning-* for create/assign events in last 90 days.
   - Step B: If event contains approval_ticket_id, follow JIRA link and attach ticket snapshot.
   - Step C: If no approval id in event, check automation logs (webhook-delivery index) for correlate trigger and lookup approver in IdP change history.
   - Final: Attach: (1) event JSON from SIEM, (2) JIRA ticket screenshot or IdP audit line, (3) time-synced S3 export proving the event was persisted.

2) Auditor: "How do you detect anomalous token sprawl / unused long-lived access?"
   - Step A: Run role-usage report: GET /reports/role-usage?window=90d.
   - Step B: Cross-reference last-used timestamp from auth-logs-* and last-grant timestamp from rbac-provisioning-*.
   - Step C: If last-used > 90d and role is scoped beyond least privilege threshold, create action item to revoke and document in role-review report.

3) Auditor: "Can you show the chain from a configuration change to deployment and its audit record?"
   - Step A: Identify change by commit SHA in config-change event (index=infra-changes-*).
   - Step B: Find CI run id and deployment id in deployment-logs-*; verify matching timestamps.
   - Step C: Attach signed deployment artifact hash and SIEM ingest line for immutable storage.

Typical troubleshooting paths (where automated evidence pipelines fail):
- Missing timestamps/mismatched clocks: check ingest-timestamp vs event.timestamp and flag host/time skew. Fix via ntp/chrony on collector nodes and reingest sample.
- SIEM index retention TTL truncated older artifacts: open ticket with observability to backfill from s3 cold storage.
- Events missing approval metadata because legacy webhook was not patched: re-run reconciliation job and attach diff report.

Gap analysis (prioritized):
- Gap 1 (high): Role attestation lacks machine-readable approval id in ~12% of assignments (root cause: legacy IdP sync). Impact: auditor follow-ups and manual evidence assembly.
  Recommended remediation: Add approval_id field to RBAC v2 events (schema v2.3), migrate webhook payloads, and add unit/integration tests. Automate detection rule in evidence-ingestion pipeline to surface new events without approval_id.
  Estimated effort: 4 engineer-weeks + 1 SRE-week for pipeline rollout.

- Gap 2 (medium): Immutable audit export retention policy for some debug artifacts currently 30 days rather than required 90 days by customer contract.
  Recommended remediation: Update S3 lifecycle, run backfill job to copy missing months to s3://audit-immutable/, and add monitoring alert on retention-policy drift.
  Owners: observability + security-ops.

- Gap 3 (low): Role-review cadence documented but not enforced; missing attestations for one business unit.
  Recommended remediation: Platform automation to create recurring role-review tasks and attach generated report to compliance ticket.

Suggested automation playbooks (short):
- Playbook: Evidence bundle generator (script)
  Inputs: control id, time window, user identifier -> Output: zipped evidence (SIEM query outputs, related JIRA tickets, signed S3 manifests).
  Implementation notes: run as ephemeral lambda with limited RBAC read-only keys, store artifact in s3 with pre-signed link for 7 days.

- Playbook: Approval-id enforcement CI job
  When: on rbactracer schema PRs and webhook config changes.
  What: run linter that fails if approval_id missing in event contract; also smoke tests against staging SIEM ingest.

Auditor Q&A bank (snippets you can paste in an auditor response):
Q: "Where are your audit logs stored and how do you protect them from tampering?"
A: "Primary logs are routed to our SIEM (index pattern: auth-logs-*, rbac-provisioning-*, infra-changes-*). Ingests write to an immutable S3 tier (s3://audit-immutable/) with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and object-lock enabled. In addition, we record object checksums in a signed manifest and surface ingest success events in the SIEM ingest-audit index. Attached: manifest sample and ingest-audit line (see evidence bundle)."

Q: "How do you demonstrate least privilege enforcement?"
A: "We provide role-review reports, automated role-usage analytics, and RBAC policy snapshots. For a sample period we attach a role-review report, effective-permissions snapshot for the role, and last-usage lines from auth logs proving scope and access frequency."

Evidence acceptance checklist (for compliance owner to run before sending to auditor):
- [ ] Query returns at least 5 concrete event samples spanning requested window.
- [ ] Each event sample includes a stable id, timestamp, and source host.
- [ ] Approval or workflow ticket id is present OR reconciliation explanation attached.
- [ ] Raw SIEM JSON + human-readable summary attached.
- [ ] Signed S3 manifest or storage checksum included for immutable evidence.

Attachment guidance (what to redact and how):
- Redact PII and long-lived credentials. Replace with stable placeholders (user: user-xxxx).
- Keep structural keys and timestamps intact; redact only values that expose customer data.
- Provide a redaction map file with the evidence bundle.

Operational play: quick runbook to respond to an auditor request (30–60 minutes):
1) Intake: compliance owner captures auditor scope & time window.
2) Run pre-built queries (RBAC provisioning, auth logs, ingest-audit) and collect top-50 hits.
3) Validate acceptance checklist. If any item fails, escalate to security-engineering with a flagged reason.
4) Create evidence bundle via script and attach redaction map.
5) Upload to secure share with expiration (pre-signed S3 link) and notify auditor with context and next steps.

Appendix: quick-reference queries (copy/paste, adapt time window):
- RBAC provisioning last 90d: siem> index=rbac-provisioning-* | where event_type in ("assign-role","revoke-role") | sort _time desc | head 50
- Auth failures by IP: siem> index=auth-logs-* | where event="login_failed" | stats count by src_ip, user
- Ingest audit for object: siem> index=ingest-audit | where object_key like "audit-immutable/%2024-09%"

Owners and escalation list:

- Observability liaison: Liam Chen (observability)
- Compliance lead: Sofia Martinez
- SRE ops (retention/backfill): Ethan Kapoor

Open action items (tracking refs):
- SC-2024: schema change to add approval_id to RBAC events (JIRA-SC-4821)
- SC-2025: backfill immutable audit for 2024-06..2024-08 (observability ticket)
- SC-2026: implement evidence-bundle lambda + pre-signed link flow

Notes / unresolved questions (for follow-up):
- Confirm IdP vendor timeline for adding approval metadata to their change logs.
- Validate whether legal requires longer pre-signed link than 7 days for certain customers.

This doc is intentionally prescriptive but remains a working draft. Please add examples, attach exported query results, and flag any additional control mappings that auditors commonly ask for.
